statusText: Tail risk is in the low band at 12% while Stress remains high at 76%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays well below the 25% block threshold because the Globex drift is small and incomplete: NQ is 0.51% under Friday's settle and its 30,717.00 session low still sits above Friday's 30,679.00 low, while ES is down only 0.34% and Japanese cash is higher. The single amplifier present is NQ holding near its own session low. The high Stress reading reflects $93.84 WTI with Brent above $106, a 5.18% 10-year and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz closure. Tail is modelled into the watch band only for the two US cash-open hours from 13:00Z to 15:00Z.
headline: NQ sets a new Globex low at 30,717.00 but holds inside Friday's range and 0.51% under settle, keeping Tail at 12%, while $93.84 WTI, Brent above $106 and an unresolved Hormuz closure hold Stress at 76%
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures are near 30,730-30,734 in the Monday Globex session, 0.51% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement, and the shape of the move is the central observation. Price opened the week at 30,870.00, pushed to 30,920.75, and has since worked steadily lower to a new session low of 30,717.00, where it currently trades about 14 points above that low. The reopen up-leg has therefore been fully retraced and the downside has extended, which is the one Tail-relevant amplifier in evidence. Two facts contain it. First, the magnitude is small: 204 points of range and roughly half a percent of net movement, and the 30,717.00 low is still above Friday's 30,679.00 low, so the entire overnight move remains a rotation inside the previous session's envelope. Second, the cross-asset tape is divergent rather than aligned. E-mini S&P futures are at 7,777.25, down only 0.34%, so the softness is index-specific rather than a broad de-risking. Japanese cash is higher, with the Nikkei 225 up 0.84% at 66,921.32 and SoftBank up 2.70%, while Korea is lower with the Kospi off 0.26% and SK Hynix down 2.09%. That split in Asian semiconductor tone is the reason the dominant mode is recorded as mixed rather than as a downtrend.

The Stress side of the assessment is where the week's difficulty sits. WTI is $93.84, up 1.55%, with a session high of $94.33, and Brent traded above $106 after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign minister has said Iran will not withdraw its conditions and no US counterproposal has been tabled, so the closure and the naval blockade remain unresolved with no published timeline. Rate levels compound that: the most recent Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, which leaves an AI-led index with little valuation cushion against an energy-driven inflation impulse. Core PCE is running at 3.3% against a 2% target and follows a recent 25 basis point increase in the policy rate. The VIX last settled at 14.87 on Friday, down 5.11%, which is the clearest single piece of evidence against a high Tail reading, although it is a Friday close rather than a live print.

The week's calendar is dense and front-loaded into the second half. JOLTS job openings and CB Consumer Confidence both land on Tuesday at 14:00Z, August core PCE together with the final second-quarter GDP estimate and ADP employment arrive on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing follows on Thursday, and September non-farm payrolls close the week on Friday at 12:30Z, with consensus near 98,000 against 162,000 previously. Roughly 22 Federal Reserve appearances are scheduled across the week, beginning with Barkin at 17:30Z today. Federal funding is secured through 11 December, so there is no month-end appropriations deadline in this window. Under the calibration this assessment applies, that event density raises Stress and constrains Confidence rather than raising Tail: importance and dispersion are not price-path evidence until an actual release produces one.

The published horizon therefore holds Tail in the low band for 22 of 24 hours and lifts it to the 20% watch band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours that contain the US cash open and the Dallas Fed release. The specific structure named for those hours is opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, which is conditional and not yet observed. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was not used as material evidence: it was collected at 00:01Z, making it roughly 145 minutes old against the 90-minute freshness limit, its collection status is partial, and both its futures and calendar sections are unavailable. All price, yield, energy and event figures above come from independent primary research performed during this run. Confidence of 76% reflects verified current futures levels and ranges from two independent sources, official yield data, verified Asian cash levels and a verified calendar, set against the absence of a live volatility or Treasury futures print.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours are covered by published Claude assessments and none has been revised. Tail stayed inside the 6%-14% low band throughout, drifting up from 6% across the quiet weekend to a 14% peak at the 23:00Z hour shortly after the Sunday futures reopen, then falling back to 9%-10% once the reopen round trip completed. Stress rose steadily from 55% to 76% over the same span as the energy and Hormuz backdrop developed, and Confidence dipped to 67% in the illiquid weekend hours before recovering to 77%-79% once live futures pricing returned. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and every hour recorded the normal dominant mode.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 02:00Z hour on 28 September through 01:00Z on 29 September. Tail is held in the low band for 22 of the 24 hours, in a 9%-15% range, and lifts to the 20% watch band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours that contain the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed release. The named structural risk for those two hours is opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, which is a conditional checkpoint rather than observed structure. Tail is lowest at 9% around the CME maintenance break and the start of the Tuesday Asian session, where liquidity is thin but the information set is settled. Stress stays in the high band throughout, peaking at 78% across the US cash open and easing to 72% overnight as the energy and rate backdrop carries forward without a new catalyst. Confidence decays from 76% to 66% across the horizon as the verified evidence gathered in this run ages. The dominant mode is recorded as mixed for every hour, reflecting a divergent rather than aligned cross-asset tape.
